sanskrit: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः । सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
hindiTranslation: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone.
essence: All human qualities arise from the same source.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Krishna says that every good and difficult human quality comes from him alone, including wisdom, restraint, joy, fear, courage, and even changes in existence itself.
simpleInsight: You do not have to manufacture your best qualities alone; they are already being carried by a larger source.
detailedMeaning: Krishna teaches more than strategy here; he is naming the source of every human capacity and condition. This verse widens the conversation from war to the whole texture of life.
modernRelevance: Before a hard talk with your father, your mood swings from courage to fear to calm to shame. Krishna's list puts every one of those states under one source, so none of them has to define you.
translationLiteral: बुद्धिः (understanding) / ज्ञानम् (wisdom) / असंमोहः (freedom from confusion) / क्षमा (forgiveness) / सत्यम् (truth) / दमः (self-restraint) / शमः (calmness) / सुखम् (pleasure) / दुःखम् (pain) / भवः (coming into being) / अभावः (ceasing to be) / भयम् (fear) / च (and) / अभयम् (fearlessness) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
insight: Forgiveness, truth, pleasure, pain, fear and fearlessness all come from Krishna, he tells Arjuna.

quoteVariants.text: Every worthy quality rises from me. Even fear and fearlessness do.
Even fear and courage come from one source.
All qualities arise from me alone.
